title: Add Hyperslate RAG step templates and AWS Tool Bridge samples
author: Nadia Ortiz
release_notes: Add Hyperslate step templates for layered RAG workflows, include an AWS Tool Bridge adapter example and sample telemetry probes; backwards-compatible examples-only change.
description:
Context: Teams building multi-step RAG workflows asked for a compact, opinionated template set that captures common retrieval -> reasoning -> tool-calling patterns while preserving observability and easy substitution of adapters. This PR introduces 'Hyperslate' — a set of lightweight step templates and orchestration helpers designed to make stepwise RAG authoring repeatable across languages and runtimes.

What this PR contains: - A new examples directory redwood-examples/rag/hyperslate-templates with TypeScript and Python templates that model common step topologies (retrieve -> prioritize -> call-tool -> synthesize). Each template includes sample input fixtures, minimal telemetry probes, and an authoring README with recommended assertions. - An AWS Tool Bridge adapter example at redwood-examples/adapters/aws-tool-bridge that demonstrates how to wire an external AWS Lambda + SQS-backed tool into a RAG step in both sync and async modes. The adapter shows auth patterns (STS role assumption example), retries, and idempotency keys. - A compact smoke harness (scripts/smoke.sh and github actions workflow .github/workflows/hyperslate-smoke.yml) used by CI to run a minimal end-to-end scenario against local mocks. - Updated docs page snippet (docs/snippets/hyperslate-getting-started.md) and a short walkthrough added to the examples index.

Motivation: Many of our customers stitch together retrieval and tool-calling without a consistent pattern for observability or failure modes. Hyperslate codifies recommended step contracts (inputs/outputs), encourages idempotent tool adapters, and includes telemetry hooks so that teams can measure latency and correctness per step. The AWS Tool Bridge sample targets customers who want a concrete pattern for integrating serverless workflows as tools.

Checklist: - [x] Add TS/Python Hyperslate templates and README examples - [x] Add AWS Tool Bridge adapter example with local mock - [x] Add CI smoke workflow and telemetry probe harness - [x] Update examples index and docs snippets - [x] Add unit tests for template validation and contract lints

Usage notes and quickstart: Clone repo, run npm install (ts template) or pip install -r requirements.txt (py template), then from redwood-examples/ run: ./scripts/smoke.sh --adapter aws-tool-bridge This spins up local mocks and exercises a short 3-step scenario. There is a separate runbook in the adapter README for configuring real AWS credentials (uses STS assume-role flow and environment variables as described).

Related work: ENG-4521 (Hyperslate templates), PM-230 (examples refresh), SUP-1284 (customer asked for serverless tool pattern).

Security notes: The AWS example includes a documented pattern for least privilege role assumption; no production credentials are checked in. The smoke harness uses mocked endpoints by default.

Compatibility: Examples are intended to be drop-in references. No runtime code in the platform is modified; changes are documentation and examples only.

Follow-ups: - Add a Go Hyperslate template in a follow-up PR (tracked ENG-4602) - Add an interactive tutorial on the docs site to guide step composition and telemetry troubleshooting.

Links: docs.redwood.dev/hyperslate (preview), linear.redwood/ENG-4521
